text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--The Confederation of Danish Industries says that the country's businesses are under-investing in research and should increase spending by 30 percent over the next five years. Current research spending by industry is about 10 billion crowns, it says.
--A Gallup poll taken after the government's new environmental taxes were announced shows a fall in consumer confidence.
--The continued growth of foreign shareholding in Danish companies means that firms will increasingly need to meet investors' demands for quick returns on capital.
--Danes should steel themselves for further rises in local authority taxes, despite central government efforts to keep them down.

--The Danish Bankers' Association believes that too few savers are investing in shares, limiting capital for future production. The bankers estimate that only 15 percent of private investment goes into the stock market.

--Danish shares have risen in value by 19 percent -- 100 billion crowns -- since the start of the year, to a total value of about 600 billion crowns. Best performer so far has been Novo Nordisk, with a rise in share value of 7.98 billion crowns.

--Social Democrat core voters earn on average about as much as Conservative and Liberal supporters, around 350,000 crowns a year, a new survey shows. It also indicates that fewer women and more of the elderly are voting Social Democrat.
